messages:
Jamal Harris: Heads up — seeing multiple customer escalations: p95/p99 generation latency jumped ~2-3x since ~22:00 UTC. Initial traces show lots of prefix cache misses and eviction churn on several nodes in eu-west-1. ETA?
Maria Gomez: Ugh. Which model/route? Any error spikes or just latency?
Jamal Harris: Mostly redwood-13B-q4 on /v1/generate. No 5xx spike, just token latency. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/p95?range=24h (red flags at 22:00). Example logs: ```2026-03-16T22:05:12Z node-42 GET /v1/generate cid=acct_789 latency=1387ms cache_hit=false prefix_key="usr:acct_789:conv:abcd" evict=true``` multiple similar lines with `cache_hit=false` and `evict=true`.
Oliver Chen: Looks like cache key cardinality explosion. Did anything change to header or prompt hashing code?
Katie Park: I pushed a normalization tweak yesterday for header ordering but it was behind a flag. Could that have toggled? PR #4621 touched prefix-key generation.
Jamal Harris: Support says ~4 distinct customers reported user-facing slowness. Repro steps from support: 1) heavy chat load 2) switched prompt template mid-session 3) latency spike. Probably different prompt text -> unique prefix keys.
Maria Gomez: If normalization isn't applied consistently, same logical prefix can map to many keys. That increases hotset entropy -> eviction thrash.
Oliver Chen: Config snapshot from affected fleet: ```prefix_cache: capacity=20k eviction_policy=lru per_prefix_limit=500 normalize=false``` which explains it. normalize=false is the culprit (we default to true on new stacks).
Katie Park: The normalization flag was flipped for the staging rollout; ops accidentally enabled the flag for some clusters but not others. There's a split brain between control plane and nodes during the rollout.
Jamal Harris: Immediate mitigations?
Maria Gomez: 1) Flip normalize=true on affected nodes (fast but must be careful with in-flight keys). 2) Increase capacity and drop per_prefix_limit to reduce thrash; e.g., capacity -> 40k, per_prefix_limit->300. 3) Warmup top N prefixes via replay to repopulate cache. 4) Route latency-SLA customers to fallback model (redwood-7B) while we stabilize.
Oliver Chen: Agree. I'll prepare a small hotfix to apply normalization and a graceful warmup. Hotfix steps: apply flag, restart prefix-cache worker with `--graceful-drain 60s`.
support-bot: Notifying affected tenants: acct_789, acct_234, acct_555. Support already opened escalations.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment starts in 2m across 3 nodes.
Katie Park: PR for normalization fix is ready. I will merge but will gate on a canary check for cache-hit rate improvement.
Jamal Harris: For warmup, use replay list we generated yesterday: `scripts/replay_prefixes --model redwood-13B-q4 --file /tmp/hot_prefixes_20260316.txt --region eu-west-1` Run at low QPS to avoid overload.
Oliver Chen: Also add a short-term policy: `prefix_cache.splay=true` to stagger warmup across nodes (cuts simultaneous evictions).
Maria Gomez: I ran a quick query: top 5000 prefixes had 90% unique hashes (no normalization). After flip, expected collisions drop, warmup will restore hit-rate.
Jamal Harris: Assignments: Maria -> coordinate normalization flip and config changes (capacity/per_prefix). Oliver -> run warmup script and monitor eviction metrics. Katie -> merge PR and observe canary. Support -> notify customers and offer fallback route. Ops -> keep an eye on autoscale.
Katie Park: Merged PR and started canary on one host. Cache hit-rate on canary went from 21% -> 62% within 4 minutes.
Oliver Chen: Warmup started (low qps). Node logs show `cache_hit=true` increasing and evict rate falling. Example: ```node-42 cache_hit_rate=0.61 evict_rate=0.04```.
Maria Gomez: Increased capacity to 40k and lowered per_prefix_limit to 300 on the remainder of the fleet.
support-bot: Tenant notifications sent. Some customers accepted fallback routing.
Jamal Harris: Monitoring: p95 in eu-west-1 trending down. Baseline was ~450ms, spike ~1200ms, now trending to ~520ms after 30m. P99 still slightly elevated.
Katie Park: P99 should recover after warmup completes and splay settles. Will keep canary and then roll.
Oliver Chen: Follow-up: schedule CR to add deterministic key normalization at the schema layer and alerting on prefix-cardinality/evict spikes. Also we need a test harness that fuzzes header ordering.
Maria Gomez: I'll draft the post-incident summary once p99 stable. For now status: mitigation applied, monitoring continuing. :white_check_mark:
